newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real rises 0.09 pct on dollar inflows.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real rises 0.09 pct on dollar inflows.

text.p: Brazil's real rose 0.09 percent to close at 1.0670 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market mostly due to dollar inflows, dealers said.
At 1640 local/1940 GMT, preliminary figures for commercial and financial forex contracts showed a $160 million surplus on Thursday.
Dealers said the supply of dollars in the market also increased because some banks decided to sell dollars after holding them in expectations of a decline in the reais-dollar mini-band.

The Central Bank lowered the mini-band Thursday by 0.09 percent to a range between 1.0670 and 1.0720 reais per dollar. So far this month, the mini-band has fallen 0.33 percent against the dollar compared to an average drop of between 0.57 and 0.61 percent in the past four months.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real fell 0.05 percent to end at 1.0716 per greenback.
In the parallel market, the real closed unchanged at 1.130 per dollar, traders said.
